items.notes: Macron called 31 Dec 'the absolute limit' for the loan. Politis cites ERT.
items.text: The extraordinary [[p:European Council]] broke up after about 14 hours without agreeing the 2028–34 budget; the planned second day was cancelled. [[p:António Costa]]'s roughly €1.78tn negotiating box is contested between seven 'frugal' states, who boycotted his small-group format, and 17 'Friends of Cohesion'. The budget and the €45bn Ukraine loan move to the 17–18 Dec summit. Costa says 24 states back the loan; Hungary, Slovakia and Czechia stay out and Bulgaria joins only the civilian strand. Eurozone leaders backed [[p:Pablo Hernández de Cos]] to succeed [[p:Christine Lagarde]] at the ECB.

items.notes: Deaths confirmed; Iranian responsibility is a Kuwaiti claim denied by Tehran.
items.reporter: Yomna Ehab, Elwely Elwelly, Angelo Amante
items.text: Italy's foreign minister said two [[p:Rheinmetall]] Italia technicians were killed when drones hit an air-defence surveillance station in Kuwait; a Pakistani worker and a Kuwaiti officer were wounded. Kuwait's defence ministry blamed Iran and said the deaths came from debris during interceptions. Iran's military denied any offensive operation and called the accusation cover for a 'false flag'. The GCC condemned the attack and [[p:Ursula von der Leyen]] called for more pressure on Iran.

items.notes: UTJ draft-law principles reported by Israeli media via Times of Israel live blog.
items.text: [[p:Gadi Eisenkot]]'s Yashar and [[p:Yair Golan]]'s Democrats agreed to sign a coalition deal after a two-day freeze over ministries, Eisenkot's second partner after [[p:Yisrael Beiteinu]] on 24 Nov. The three parties hold 36 seats, well short of 61; [[p:Naftali Bennett]]'s 12-seat list has not signed. Israeli media report Yashar and UTJ agreed principles of a Haredi draft law. Eisenkot's mandate runs to 6 Dec, extendable by 14 days.

items.notes: Strike warning is a Ukrainian government claim. Meduza confirms the nuclear and restraint remarks, not the deadlock line.
items.text: [[p:Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] said intelligence shows Russia is completing preparations for a new mass strike on energy and logistics, and asked for more Patriot interceptors, scarce since the Iran war. US envoy [[p:Jared Kushner]] said talks are at 'a little bit of a deadlock' over territory and that [[p:Vladimir Putin]] had agreed not to use nuclear weapons and shown 'restraint'. [[p:Donald Trump]] urged Putin to pull back military aggression.

items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: Figures are Ukrainian official. Borderline Tier 1; context for the strike warning.
items.text: Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 155 drones overnight into 27 Nov, with 110 downed or suppressed and hits at 27 locations; one person was killed and at least 16 injured in Zaporizhzhia, and energy and rail sites in Vinnytsia and Zhytomyr were hit, cutting power in six regions. Estonia issued an air-threat warning for six counties and NATO jets were scrambled; no airspace violation was confirmed.

items.notes: Jazan death per Saudi government; 50-target figure is a coalition claim; Ras Tanura claim is Houthi.
items.text: Saudi state media said a [[p:Houthis|Houthi]] strike on the Jazan refinery killed a Nepalese worker and briefly halted some operations. Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki said the coalition then destroyed 50 military targets in Sanaa, Hodeidah and Saada, including the launcher used against Jazan. The Houthis claimed attacks on Jeddah and Jazan ports and Ras Tanura; the coalition reported interceptions and did not confirm a Ras Tanura hit.

items.notes: KCNA account plus AP reporting; no independent second outlet found.
items.text: State media said [[p:Kim Jong Un]] inspected two nuclear-materials factories, one new and one expanding, plus a nuclear-powered equipment base and a research institute, calling the arsenal irreversible and battlefield low-yield weapons urgent; he named South Korea the 'most dangerous enemy state'. Seoul's defence ministry said it takes the remarks seriously; [[p:Rafael Grossi]] called the Yongbyon enrichment expansion a cause for serious concern.

items.notes: Single intelligence source (HUR); treat with caution.
items.text: Ukraine's military intelligence claims North Korea has temporarily suspended military aid to Russia after Moscow offered in October to mediate between the two Koreas, including halting KN-23 missile and shell deliveries and delaying a Russian request to expand the troop contingent. Neither Moscow nor Pyongyang has confirmed it.

items.notes: Xinhua link covers only the defence ministry remarks.
items.text: Japan's coast guard says two [[p:China Coast Guard]] ships entered waters near the Senkakus and tried to approach a Japanese fishing boat, the fifth such approach this year; Beijing said it lodged representations and took 'necessary control measures'. China's defence ministry separately accused Japan of fuelling South China Sea tensions by supplying radars and drones to the Philippines.

items.notes: China and Brazil positions confirmed; EU, Japan, Singapore, Vietnam reactions from a secondary roundup only. Brazil source in Portuguese.
items.reporter: Zhang Chenxu, Zhong Nan, Lia Zhu
items.text: China's commerce ministry called the proposed [[e:Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974|Section 301]] tariffs typical unilateralism and reserved the right to respond; Brazil said it will not yield and did not rule out a WTO case or reciprocal measures. European Parliament trade chair [[p:Bernd Lange]] reportedly called the 20% EU rate absurd; Japan, Singapore and Vietnam also objected.
